findings.explanation: The module call sets key_id to the pre-existing key projects/.../keyRings/pangpt_kms_key_ring/cryptoKeys/pangpt_kms_crypto (in us-central1), but the KMS IAM binding grants the GCF service agent access to google_kms_crypto_key.pike (in europe-west2) — a completely different key. The service agent cannot access the key the function is actually encrypted with, so deployment will fail. Additionally, the role is roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypter (encrypt-only); the GCF service agent requires roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter to both encrypt and decrypt function artifacts. Two independent bugs on the same resource, both blocking deployment.
findings.title: KMS IAM grant is on the wrong key and insufficient role — function deployment will fail

findings.explanation: The service_config block does not set ingress_settings. The Google provider default is ALLOW_ALL, meaning the function URL is reachable from the public internet. HLD_GCP_021 (Cloud Functions must restrict ingress to internal traffic only) passed because the attribute is absent and the engine cannot evaluate a missing field. The function is only invoked by Cloud Scheduler; it should be ALLOW_INTERNAL_ONLY to prevent the endpoint being reachable from arbitrary internet hosts (even though IAM auth is still required, the endpoint surface is unnecessarily exposed).
findings.remediation: Add ingress_settings = "ALLOW_INTERNAL_ONLY" inside the service_config block in google_cloudfunctions2_function.tf.
findings.title: service_config.ingress_settings omitted — function defaults to ALLOW_ALL, HLD_GCP_021 blind spot
